items.summary: Recommendation: maintain financial containment. Do not approve new spend, scale AI usage, or make revenue, ROI, contribution-margin, or forecast claims. Amazon evidence covers only 2026-09-21: 6,219 clicks, 28 ordered items, 6 shipped items, and $4.92 aggregate commission under an unattributed row; named site rows show $0 site-attributed commission. September AI usage is 5,531 calls costing $1,002.46, including 234 errors (4.23%); cost per validated output is not calculable because calls are not mapped to accepted work or revenue. Keep existing capacity and launch gates unchanged until a report-only finance baseline reconciles revenue, AI cost, infrastructure cost, and attributable work.

Finance disposition: preserve the existing affiliate-attribution control. The 2026-09-21 Amazon aggregate row contains 629 clicks, 28 ordered items, 6 shipped items, and $4.92 commission that cannot be assigned to a site. Require every new affiliate link to use a registered tracking ID, but do not represent tracking coverage as revenue attribution. No duplicate telemetry request is needed.

Cost-to-learn conclusion: AI spend is measurable, but learning efficiency is not. September cost per AI call is approximately $0.1812 ($1,002.46 / 5,531), while cost per error is approximately $4.28 ($1,002.46 / 234); neither is a unit-economic or contribution-margin metric. A validated cost-to-learn figure requires work-item-level AI cost, accepted-output status, measurement result, and attributable revenue or avoided cost.
